title: Crispy pork, potato and salad leaf bowls

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a plain cupboard staple such as cider vinegar and wholegrain mustard, with no factory-made sauces or mixes.

supermarket.reason: New potatoes, pork shoulder, salad leaves, apples and radishes are all everyday items at Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a bowl, a knife and a whisk or fork, with simple roasting and tossing.

works.reason: Halved new potatoes get 45 minutes at 220°C and thin pork strips get 25 minutes, so both will be cooked and crisp, and 500g pork with 750g potatoes suits four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is realistic for halving potatoes, cutting the pork into strips, slicing the apples and radishes and making the dressing, and the 20 plus 25 minutes of roasting matches the 45 printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, nothing unlisted is used, and the oil adds up (1 tbsp on the potatoes, the remaining 2 in the dressing).

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm salad with garden leaves, radishes and chives suits an early April lunch, and the 250g of leaves form the base of each bowl rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pork, potatoes, leaves, apple and radish make a balanced, filling meal a family would happily eat again.
